before_codex: Inspect current repository/evidence and use available ChatGPT Classic reasoning and connectors/tools.
Attempt bounded self-resolution and alternate supported tool paths.
Use role-first consultation for ambiguity, missing evidence, software/design questions, or suspected cheating.
Prove the remaining blocker is an execution capability unavailable in ChatGPT Classic.
codex_allowed_only_for: local checkout or shell execution unavailable in ChatGPT Classic
repository tests/builds/benchmarks that must run in an unavailable local environment
interactive authenticated developer tooling not exposed to ChatGPT Classic
a code mutation that cannot be performed safely with available Classic/GitHub tooling after bounded attempts
codex_prompt: Delegate only the smallest blocked subtask. Keep the prompt token-aware and include repository, node, exact base SHA when relevant, exact scope, exact task/commands, evidence to return, and stop condition. Do not restate the whole plan. Return evidence to ChatGPT Classic, which remains node owner.
human_instructions: Never assume the user knows how to perform a manual action. Give exact click-by-click UI steps or copy-paste commands, what should appear, exactly what to send back, and safety/rollback guidance when relevant.
human_rule: Ask the user only for genuine human authority/access after Classic tools, self-resolution, role consultation, and any truly necessary bounded Codex subtask are exhausted.

response_contract.blocks_rule: List a blocker only after self-resolution paths are exhausted. State what was tried, why it remains blocked, and whether a bounded Codex subtask or genuine human action is required. Use None. when clear.

scope: all nodes and all dispatcher/repair/reconciliation/integration/promotion/replan work in this plan
